name: rotate_blend_by_tool
description: Reference-parity: the rotate falloff blend is selected BY TOOL, not by axis count. Every case here is a SINGLE-axis rotation that nevertheless takes the MATRIX-LERP arm ((1-w)I + w*R, radii shrinking to a minimum of cos(theta/2)), because the tool is the unified transform. Read them against softrotate.json's rot_lin_90, which is the same 90-degree rotation under the same radial linear falloff on the same seg-4 cube via the soft-rotate preset, and which preserves every radius exactly. The rival law -- that the arm is chosen by AXIS COUNT -- predicts the arc arm for all of these and is refuted by each of them. Before this suite the whole rotate corpus was single-axis-arc plus multi-axis-lerp, which IS the rival's partition and so could not tell the two laws apart.
source: Frozen reference capture (radial falloff, real-GL session; capture via the private capture tooling).

provenance.harness: private capture tooling (generator script outside tools/local/fixture_gen/)
provenance.notes: Single axis, yet matrix-lerp -- which is what the axis-count rival cannot produce. The arc twin is softrotate.json's rot_lin_90 (same angle, same falloff, same mesh, different tool); it is referenced rather than copied so one measurement keeps one home.
